subject: Week 25: start the open cup — visit window closes Nov 9
bodyText:
This week
Days 173-179 widen the menu: 10-15 foods is a typical running total, with acceptance swinging day to day. Independent sitting is arriving for some and rocking on hands and knees can emerge — the CDC checkpoint for sitting without support is 9 months, so neither is due yet. Expect long 'mamama' and 'bababa' babble strings and a real reaction when you leave the room.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] A food accepted Tuesday is refused Thursday — expect 5-10 exposures before a new food lands.
- [monitor] Refusal across whole food categories, or flat weight since starting solids — bring both to the pediatrician.
- [call within 24h] Diarrhea persisting past three days, or a new wheeze or lingering cough.
- [call now] Fever of 102F rectal or higher with marked lethargy — same-day call, ER if he is hard to rouse.

Enrichment opportunities
- Offer an open cup (or straw cup) at each meal — the AAP puts cup introduction around 6 months with full bottle retirement by 12-18 months, and open beats spouted for oral-motor development. Keep the allergen rotation running at 2-3x weekly per allergen in parallel. AAP: Starting Solid Foods: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Starting-Solid-Foods.aspx
- Take him to the California Academy of Sciences on a rainy morning — the aquarium floor is slow-moving, high-contrast visual tracking at stroller height, and a reliable recurring sensory outing for the wet season. California Academy of Sciences: https://www.calacademy.org/
- Anchor a morning song and a different bedtime song — a consistent audio cue at each end of the day reinforces the sleep routine you already run. AAP: infant sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/default.aspx
- Stage toys just out of reach during floor and tummy time — pivoting, then commando crawling, is the usual sequence, and reach practice is the input you control. AAP: Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Shoot the 6-month tripod-sit portrait — solo on a blanket, same backdrop as the 100-day shot, for the comparison stack.

Upcoming
- Day 168-182 (Oct 26–Nov 9, 2026): 6-month well visit window closes Nov 9 — last call to book. Influenza #1 needs a second dose four weeks later in a first season; calendar it on the way out.
- Day 180 (Nov 7, 2026): the 6-month program windows open — swim converts to paid, ISR instructor lists open, Suzuki instrument decision due. Next week's email carries the full brief.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Supports whole weight on legs when held standing
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Builds leg strength for eventual pulling-to-stand. Does not need to bear weight independently.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/supports-weight-on-legs/complete

- Moves things from one hand to the other
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Bilateral coordination across the midline. Often accompanied by mouthing the transferred object.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/transfers-objects-hand-to-hand/complete

- Closes lips to show she doesn't want more food
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Pre-verbal refusal. Important to respect — supports developing satiety cues.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/closes-lips-not-more/complete

- Enjoys back-and-forth social play
  AAP window: day 150-240
  What to look for: Active turn-taking in physical or vocal games. Distinct from earlier passive enjoyment of stimulation.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-7-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/enjoys-social-play/complete

- Sits without support
  AAP window: day 150-270
  What to look for: Hands free for play. WHO motor study cites 3.8-9.2 mo as the typical range.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/sits-without-support/complete
